text: Hello, Bonansians, let's talk about limit orders. A limit order is an order that you place on the order book that will be executed at the price you determine or better. So you place limit orders if you're on this buying side, the lower side of the buy book, or the higher side of the sell book, it allows you to buy at a cheaper price or sell at a higher price. Also, when you use limit orders and they're placed on the order book and they're not executed immediately as a market order is, you save on fees as a market maker. So how do you use it? Well, let's say I want to sell my BNB at a higher price than is currently being bid. So I just come over here, perhaps above this cell wall, click on this number which is loaded in here, and I say I would like to sell 100% of my Binance coin. Click on Sell BNB and boom, it's done. We have a confirmation. We can scroll down to our open orders and we can see right here that I have a limit order to sell BNB once it reaches this height. And you can see my order here is designated by the small arrow. So that's how you use it when you should use it. Well, if you're coming in and you're not in a rush to place a market order and you want to get just a little bit better price, you can use it if you want to buy, for example, at a major support line or if you want to sell at a major resistance line, and that's how you use a limit order.
